definition.title: What is the Astorian currency?
definition.lead: The Astorian currency is the Republic's unit of account: it measures values, makes exchanges easier and allows saving. Issued by the Central Bank, it is the foundation of the national economy.

paragraphs.p1: The Astorian currency is the official currency of the Republic of Astoria. It performs three inseparable functions — counting, exchanging, saving — that make it the central instrument of any economy.
paragraphs.p2: Issued by the Central Bank of Astoria, it is accepted throughout the territory. Its status, issue and stability are governed by monetary law and by the action of the BCA.

unite.title: A unit of account
unite.text: All prices, contracts and claims are expressed in the same unit: the Astorian franc.

echange.title: A medium of exchange
echange.text: Accepted by everyone, it makes it possible to buy and sell without bartering.

reserve.title: A store of value
reserve.text: It preserves purchasing power over time, provided it remains stable.

unite.title: The Astorian franc and its subdivisions
unite.lead: The monetary unit is the common reference for all prices and payments. The Astorian franc is a decimal unit, divided into centimes.

paragraphs.p1: A decimal unit simplifies calculations and the comparison of prices. Centimes make it possible to express retail prices precisely without ever losing the common reference.

official.title: The official status of the Astorian franc
official.lead: The Astorian franc is the only currency with legal tender throughout the territory of the Republic.

paragraphs.p1: The official currency is the expression of the monetary sovereignty of the Republic. Only the law can define the national currency, entrust its issue and change its status: this framework gives it strength and legitimacy.
paragraphs.p2: The Central Bank of Astoria issues banknotes; coins are minted by the Public Treasury under state control. No other authority may issue legal-tender money.

emission.title: Who issues the Astorian currency?
emission.lead: Issuing the national currency is the first privilege of the Central Bank. It is distinct from the creation of bank money by commercial banks.

paragraphs.p1: The Central Bank of Astoria issues fiat money — banknotes — and central bank money, the only money it controls directly. It organises the putting into circulation of cash and guarantees the liquidity of the banking system.
paragraphs.p2: Most of the money in circulation is not issued by the BCA: it is created by commercial banks when they grant loans. The BCA frames this creation through its monetary policy and its regulation.

pouvoirLiberatoire.title: What legal tender power means
pouvoirLiberatoire.lead: Legal tender power is the legal force of money: paying in Astorian francs discharges the debtor's debt.

paragraphs.p1: Money has legal tender power when it releases the debtor from their obligation. Accepting francs means being certain of being able to settle one's own debts in turn: this is the foundation of trust in money.
paragraphs.p2: Legal tender power must not be confused with legal tender: legal tender obliges the creditor to accept the money, legal tender power guarantees that it actually discharges the debt.

bullets.b1: Banknotes have legal tender power with no amount limit for debts denominated in francs.
bullets.b2: Coins have legal tender power within the limits set by law.
bullets.b3: Cash payments may be capped for certain transactions, notably to combat money laundering.

pouvoirLiberatoire.notice: The exact caps and exceptions are set by law and detailed in the implementing texts published in the Official Journal.

cadre.title: The actors of the Astorian currency
cadre.lead: The Astorian currency sits within an institutional framework that clearly separates monetary issue, monetary policy and fiscal policy.

paragraphs.p1: The Republic sets the legal framework; the Central Bank issues money and conducts monetary policy; the Public Treasury manages the accounts and treasury of the State; banks distribute money and create scriptural money. Each exercises its role without confusion.

stabilite.title: Monetary stability, a responsibility of the Central Bank
stabilite.lead: Money is stable when its purchasing power holds over time. This stability is the primary mission of monetary policy.

paragraphs.p1: Monetary stability rests on confidence: confidence in the value of money, in its authenticity and in the Central Bank's ability to stay the course. It is measured first by price stability.
paragraphs.p2: To preserve it, the Central Bank acts on its key rates and on the liquidity of the banking system. Controlled inflation protects the purchasing power of households and safeguards savings.

economie.title: From money to monetary policy
economie.lead: Money connects all the actors of the economy: it circulates from banks to households and businesses, supports payments and feeds monetary policy.

paragraphs.p1: Understanding the Astorian currency means understanding a sequence: money is issued, distributed by banks, used for payments, irrigates the economy, and its evolution guides monetary policy decisions.

securite.title: The security features of banknotes
securite.lead: Each banknote incorporates devices that can be checked by sight, touch and movement. They are the first line of defence against counterfeiting.

paragraphs.p1: The security features combine: some are visible, others are felt, others appear only when the note is tilted or under ultraviolet light.

papier.text: Special, resistant and slightly crackling paper, distinct from ordinary paper.

relief.title: The reliefs
relief.text: Raised inks can be felt on the main motif and the name of the bank.

filigrane.title: The watermark
filigrane.text: Visible against the light, it reproduces a motif that lightens as the note is tilted.

fenetre.title: The transparent window
fenetre.text: A window letting light through, with details that move according to the viewing angle.

impression.title: The two-sided printing
impression.text: Both sides form an exact motif when observed against the light.

fluorescence.title: Fluorescent inks
fluorescence.text: Under ultraviolet light, coloured elements appear on the face of the note.

microtexte.text: Tiny text, sharp under a magnifier but unreadable to the naked eye.

barcode.title: The barcode and number
barcode.text: A barcode and a numbered series allow the traceability of notes.

authentifier.title: Authenticate a banknote in four steps
authentifier.lead: Without any instrument, the four-step method lets anyone check the authenticity of a banknote.

paragraphs.p1: Touch, look, tilt, check: this simple sequence covers the main security features and detects most counterfeits.

toucher.title: Touch
toucher.text: Feel the paper and the reliefs: a real note is firm, crisp and its raised inks can be felt.

regarder.title: Look
regarder.text: Check the watermark against the light and the two-sided printing coincidence.

incliner.title: Tilt
incliner.text: Tilt the note: the transparent window and the changing motifs confirm authenticity.

controler.title: Check
controler.text: If in doubt, compare with a known note and hand the suspect note to your bank.

cycle.title: Issue, withdrawal and replacement
cycle.lead: Cash is born, circulates, wears out and is then withdrawn and replaced. This cycle is run by the Central Bank and the Public Treasury.

paragraphs.p1: Cash leaves the Central Bank's vaults for the banks, then for the public. It then returns to the BCA, which sorts and checks it.
paragraphs.p2: The withdrawal calendar and exchange conditions are announced publicly by the Central Bank.

cycle.notice: A damaged but authentic note keeps its value and can be exchanged under the published conditions.

pratiques.title: Using cash every day
pratiques.lead: Cash remains an accessible and immediate means of payment. A few good practices make it easier to use.

paragraphs.p1: Cash has legal tender throughout the territory. Storing it well and knowing how to check it protects all users.
paragraphs.p2: In case of a suspect note, never put it back into circulation: hand it to your bank or the authorities.

conservation.title: Store
conservation.text: Keep banknotes flat and away from moisture to keep them in good condition.

acceptation.title: Have it accepted
acceptation.text: A merchant cannot refuse Astorian francs for a debt denominated in that currency.

contrefacon.title: Counterfeiting
contrefacon.text: Everyone's vigilance protects the authenticity of money.

vision.title: How money circulates
vision.lead: Money circulates constantly between the Central Bank, banks, businesses, households and the State. Understanding this circuit means understanding how money is born, circulates and is withdrawn.

paragraphs.p1: Monetary circulation refers to all the movements of money in the economy. It includes fiat money — banknotes and coins — and scriptural money, recorded in bank accounts.
paragraphs.p2: These two forms are complementary: cash handles immediate everyday payments, while scriptural money carries most transactions, wages and settlements between businesses.

creation.title: Creation
creation.text: Money is born from the Central Bank's operations and banks' lending.

especes.title: Cash
especes.text: Banknotes and coins pass from hand to hand for current payments.

scripturale.title: Scriptural money
scripturale.text: Deposits circulate by transfer, card and direct debit.

creation.title: Central money and bank money
creation.lead: Money is not created in a single place: the Central Bank issues central money, while banks create scriptural money through credit.

paragraphs.p1: Central bank money is the safest money in the system: it is held by banks as reserves and used for their settlements between themselves and with the Central Bank.
paragraphs.p2: Bank money is born from credit: when a bank grants a loan, it simultaneously records a deposit in favour of the borrower. Each repayment destroys money. This process is framed by monetary policy and prudential regulation.

emissionEspeces.title: The issue and putting into circulation of cash
emissionEspeces.lead: The Central Bank is at the heart of cash issue: it orders banknotes, organises their delivery and guarantees their authenticity.

paragraphs.p1: Banknotes are printed under the control of the Central Bank, which sets their characteristics and security features. Coins are minted by the Public Treasury.
paragraphs.p2: Cash is stored in the BCA's vaults before being made available to banks, which supply their branches and ATMs.

bca.text: It orders banknotes and organises the putting into circulation of cash.

tresor.title: The Public Treasury

circulationEspeces.title: The path of cash
circulationEspeces.lead: Cash follows a continuous circuit between the Central Bank, banks and the public.

paragraphs.p1: The Central Bank supplies banks, which make cash available to businesses and individuals. It then returns to the banks, then to the BCA to be sorted and checked.

circulationEspeces.notice: Cash in circulation is subject to authenticity checks throughout the circuit.

scripturale.title: Deposits and electronic payments
scripturale.lead: Scriptural money is the money recorded in accounts: it circulates by transfer, card and direct debit, without a physical medium.

paragraphs.p1: Opening an account means holding scriptural money. Payments between accounts, transfers and direct debits move this money from one institution to another, through the payment infrastructures.
paragraphs.p2: Movements between institutions are settled in central bank money: banks exchange reserves on the accounts they hold at the BCA.

bullets.b1: Bank accounts carry scriptural money.
bullets.b2: Sight and savings deposits make up most of the money.
bullets.b3: Electronic payments move deposits between accounts.
bullets.b4: Transfers between banks are settled in central bank money.

banques.title: The role of banks in circulation
banques.lead: Banks are the central intermediaries of money: they collect deposits, grant credit and distribute cash.

paragraphs.p1: By collecting deposits and granting credit, banks create scriptural money and keep it circulating.
paragraphs.p2: They must at all times hold sufficient liquidity and reserves to meet withdrawals and settlements.

depots.title: Collecting deposits
depots.text: Household and business deposits finance activity.

liquidite.title: Managing liquidity
liquidite.text: Banks must meet withdrawals and settlements.

reserves.title: Holding reserves
reserves.text: Reserves are held on accounts at the BCA.

retrait.title: Withdrawal, checking and destruction
retrait.lead: Cash wears out: it returns to the Central Bank, is checked and then withdrawn and replaced.

paragraphs.p1: Banks return the cash they receive to the Central Bank. The BCA sorts it, checks its authenticity, puts notes in good condition back into circulation and withdraws those that are too worn.
paragraphs.p2: Withdrawn notes are replaced by new ones, and worn coins are melted down by the Public Treasury.

retrait.notice: Withdrawn notes keep their legal tender power for an announced period, then can be exchanged under the published conditions.

mesurer.title: Measuring monetary circulation
mesurer.lead: Monetary circulation is measured by quantity and value indicators: cash outstanding, money supply and aggregates.

paragraphs.p1: These indicators shed light on the importance of cash and scriptural money in the economy, and on their evolution over time.

hero.title: The official currency
hero.lead: The Republic of Astoria has a single currency, the only one with legal tender throughout the territory: the Astorian franc.

cadre.title: The currency of the Republic
cadre.lead: The Astorian franc is established by monetary law, which sets its name, unit and conditions of issue.

paragraphs.p1: The official currency expresses the monetary sovereignty of the Republic. Only the law can define the national currency, entrust its issue and modify its status: it is this framework that gives money its solidity and legitimacy.
paragraphs.p2: The Central Bank of Astoria is responsible for issuing banknotes, and the Public Treasury for striking coins. No other authority may issue legal-tender money.
paragraphs.p3: Provisional denomination: the official name and reference characteristics will be published by the Central Bank.

cadre.notice: The exact status of the official currency is defined by monetary law, whose consolidated text is published in the Official Journal.

coursLegal.title: What is legal tender?
coursLegal.lead: Legal tender obliges any creditor to accept the national currency in payment of a debt expressed in that currency.

paragraphs.p1: Saying that a currency is legal tender means that it must be accepted as a means of payment on the national territory. A trader cannot refuse Astorian francs to settle a purchase, except in cases provided for by law.
paragraphs.p2: This principle protects monetary unity: it guarantees that all prices, wages and contracts are expressed in the same currency and that every citizen can pay and be paid everywhere.

bullets.b1: Payment in the national currency extinguishes the debt, within the limits set for each means of payment.
bullets.b2: The national currency cannot be refused for transactions denominated in francs.
bullets.b3: Rounding and change rules apply in accordance with the law.

payer.title: Paying
payer.text: You can pay in cash anywhere in the country, free of charge, within the applicable limits.

etrePaye.title: Being paid
etrePaye.text: Salaries, benefits and reimbursements are expressed in Astorian francs.

epargner.title: Saving
epargner.text: Your deposits and investments are denominated in the national currency.

echanger.title: Exchanging
echanger.text: Exchanges with foreign currencies are offered by banking institutions.

statut.title: Legal status
statut.lead: The status of the official currency is defined by monetary law.

paragraphs.p1: The law sets the name, the unit, the issuer and the legal tender of the national currency.

cours.label: Legal tender
cours.value: Throughout the territory of the Republic

territoire.title: The territory of circulation
territoire.lead: The Astorian franc circulates throughout the territory of the Republic.

paragraphs.p1: Legal tender applies everywhere in Astoria, without territorial exception.
paragraphs.p2: Exchanges with abroad are subject to specific exchange rules.

relation.title: The relation with the Republic
relation.lead: Money is an institution of the sovereignty of the Republic.

paragraphs.p1: Only the Republic, by law, can define the national currency and entrust its issue.
paragraphs.p2: The Central Bank exercises this mandate in full independence, within the framework set by law.

reconnaissance.title: Institutional recognition
reconnaissance.lead: The Astorian currency is recognised as the only legal-tender currency.

paragraphs.p1: Prices, wages, contracts and public accounts are all expressed in Astorian francs.
paragraphs.p2: This recognition guarantees monetary unity and the legibility of the economy.

meta.title: The monetary unit
meta.description: The Astorian monetary unit: the franc, its subdivisions in centimes, its role as a unit of account and the reasons for a single unit.

hero.title: The monetary unit
hero.lead: The monetary unit is the common reference of all prices and payments in Astoria: the franc, divided into centimes.

leFrancEtSesSubdivisions.title: The franc and its subdivisions
leFrancEtSesSubdivisions.lead: The Astorian monetary system is based on a decimal unit: one franc equals one hundred centimes.

table.caption: The units of the Astorian currency

paragraphs.p1: Choosing a decimal unit simplifies calculations and the comparison of prices. The subdivision into centimes makes it possible to express retail prices finely without ever losing the common reference.

uniteDeCompte.title: A unit that counts
uniteDeCompte.lead: The franc is the standard to which all prices, contracts and claims are referenced.

paragraphs.p1: The monetary unit is first of all a unit of account: it serves to measure the value of goods and services, to compare prices and to denominate contracts and debts. Without a common unit of account, no economy could coordinate itself.
paragraphs.p2: This is why public statistics, the State budget and company accounts are all expressed in the same unit, making economic information legible and comparable.

uneUniteUnique.title: The reasons for a single unit

simplicite.title: Simplicity
simplicite.text: A single standard makes prices comparable throughout the country.

confiance.title: Confidence
confiance.text: A single, stable currency protects purchasing power.

integration.title: Integration
integration.text: It facilitates exchanges between regions and sectors of the economy.

stabilite.title: Stability
stabilite.text: The monetary policy of the Central Bank watches over its value.

symbole.title: The symbol and the notation
symbole.lead: The Astorian franc is written FAS, and its centimes written c.

paragraphs.p1: The notation of money follows precise conventions to avoid any ambiguity.

subdivisions.title: The subdivisions
subdivisions.lead: The franc is divided into one hundred centimes.

paragraphs.p1: The decimal subdivision simplifies calculations and the comparison of prices.
paragraphs.p2: Centimes make it possible to express retail prices precisely.

bullets.b1: One franc is worth one hundred centimes.
bullets.b2: Coins cover the subdivisions from the centime to the franc.
bullets.b3: Prices are displayed with two decimals.

affichage.title: Display conventions
affichage.lead: The display of amounts follows uniform conventions throughout the territory.

paragraphs.p1: Amounts are written with a thousands separator and two decimals.
paragraphs.p2: These conventions apply to prices, accounts and official documents.

bullets.b1: Thousands separator: space.
bullets.b2: Decimal separator: comma.
bullets.b3: Two decimals for centimes.

usages.title: Common uses
usages.lead: The franc is the reference unit for all economic exchanges.

paragraphs.p1: Prices, wages, accounts and contracts are all expressed in the same unit.

prix.title: Prices
prix.text: All goods and services are displayed in francs.

comptes.title: Accounts
comptes.text: Public and private accounting uses the franc.

contrats.title: Contracts
contrats.text: Commitments are expressed in the monetary unit.

approfondir.lead: The monetary unit is understood with the official status and cash.

meta.title: Issued by the Central Bank
meta.description: The issue privilege of the Central Bank of Astoria: how the BCA issues banknotes, creates central bank money and controls money.

hero.title: Issued by the Central Bank
hero.lead: The Central Bank of Astoria is the only authority authorised to issue the banknotes of the Republic: this is the issue privilege.

privilege.title: The issue privilege
privilege.lead: Issuing the national currency is one of the fundamental privileges of the Central Bank.

paragraphs.p1: The issue privilege gives the Central Bank the exclusive right to issue legal-tender banknotes. It is the counterpart of its mission: to guarantee confidence in money and the stability of its value.
paragraphs.p2: This monopoly prevents the proliferation of competing currencies and ensures the monetary unity of the Republic. Banknotes issued by the BCA bear its signature and are the only fiduciary means of payment with legal tender.

comment.title: How the Central Bank issues money
comment.lead: Issue takes several forms, all controlled by the Central Bank.

billets.title: Banknotes
billets.text: Printed under its control, they bear the security features and its signature.

monnaieCentrale.title: Central bank money
monnaieCentrale.text: Created during refinancing operations, it is held in reserve by the banks.

comptes.title: Accounts
comptes.text: Credit institutions hold their reserves in the BCA's accounts.

controle.title: Control
controle.text: The BCA regulates the monetary creation of banks through its instruments and its regulation.

paragraphs.p1: Banknotes leave the printing works for the Central Bank's vaults, then for commercial banks which supply their cash machines and counters. Cash then returns to the BCA, which sorts it, verifies its authenticity and puts it back into circulation or withdraws it.
paragraphs.p2: Scriptural money, for its part, circulates first on the accounts of the banks: each credit granted creates money, each repayment destroys it. The Central Bank regulates this process by setting the cost of central bank money.

billets.title: Banknotes, the signature of the BCA
billets.lead: Astorian banknotes bear the signature of the Central Bank, a guarantee of their authenticity.

paragraphs.p1: The BCA is the only authority allowed to issue legal-tender banknotes.
paragraphs.p2: Each banknote incorporates security features and the signature of the Central Bank.

monnaieCentrale.title: Central bank money
monnaieCentrale.lead: Central bank money is the safest money in the system.

paragraphs.p1: It is created by the Central Bank during its refinancing operations.
paragraphs.p2: It serves as the foundation for bank reserves and interbank settlements.

nature.label: Nature
nature.value: Money issued by the Central Bank

detenteurs.label: Holders
detenteurs.value: Banks, on their accounts at the BCA

comptes.title: Bank accounts at the BCA
comptes.lead: Banks hold their reserves on the accounts they open at the Central Bank.

paragraphs.p1: These accounts enable settlements between banks in central bank money.
paragraphs.p2: They are the interface between the Central Bank and the banking system.

controle.title: Controlling money creation
controle.lead: The Central Bank frames the money creation of banks.

paragraphs.p1: Through its key rates and instruments, the BCA influences the cost and quantity of central bank money.

bullets.b1: Key rates steer the cost of money.
bullets.b2: Required reserves frame bank liquidity.
bullets.b3: Refinancing operations provide the needed liquidity.

controle.notice: This control takes place within the framework of the Republic's monetary policy.

missions.title: The missions of the BCA
missions.lead: The issue of money fits into the full set of missions of the Central Bank.

meta.title: Legal tender power
meta.description: The legal tender power of the Astorian currency: what the law provides, how it applies in practice and the limits of cash.

hero.title: Legal tender power
hero.lead: Legal tender power is the legal force of money: it extinguishes any debt expressed in the national currency.

paragraphs.p1: A currency has legal tender power when it frees the debtor from his obligation: paying in the national currency extinguishes the debt, whatever its value. This is the foundation of confidence in money: everyone knows that by accepting francs, they will be able to settle their own debts.
paragraphs.p2: Legal tender power must not be confused with legal tender. Legal tender obliges accepting the currency; legal tender power guarantees that it actually pays the debt.

laLoi.title: What the law provides
laLoi.lead: Legal tender power is exercised according to precise rules, which distinguish banknotes from coins.

bullets.b1: Banknotes have legal tender power without amount limit for debts denominated in francs.
bullets.b2: Coins have legal tender power within the limits set by law, beyond which the creditor may refuse a payment made exclusively in coins.
bullets.b3: Cash payments may be capped for certain transactions, with a view to combating money laundering.
bullets.b4: Legal tender power applies only to payments in the national currency.

laLoi.notice: The exact limits are set by law and specified in the implementing texts published in the Official Journal.

enPratique.title: Legal tender power in daily life

acheter.title: Buying
acheter.text: Settle your purchases in cash within the payment limits.

rembourser.title: Repaying
rembourser.text: A payment in francs extinguishes your debt, whatever its source.

recevoir.title: Receiving
recevoir.text: You cannot be forced to accept another currency in payment.

echanger.title: Exchanging
echanger.text: Withdrawn banknotes keep their value during the withdrawal period.

billets.title: The legal tender power of banknotes
billets.lead: Banknotes have legal tender power with no amount limit.

paragraphs.p1: For debts denominated in francs, a payment in banknotes discharges the debt, whatever its amount.
paragraphs.p2: This is one of the fundamental guarantees of the Astorian currency.

pieces.title: The legal tender power of coins
pieces.lead: Coins have legal tender power limited to the amounts set by law.

paragraphs.p1: Beyond these amounts, a creditor may refuse a payment made only in coins.
paragraphs.p2: This limit does not call into question the value of coins, which remain exchangeable.

limites.title: Limits and exceptions
limites.lead: Legal tender power has a few limits provided by law.

bullets.b1: Coins are limited to the amounts set by law.
bullets.b2: Cash payments may be capped for certain transactions.
bullets.b3: Transactions with abroad follow exchange rules.
bullets.b4: Legal tender power applies only to the national currency.

coursLegal.title: Legal tender power and legal tender
coursLegal.lead: Legal tender and legal tender power are two complementary notions.

paragraphs.p1: Legal tender obliges the creditor to accept the national currency.
paragraphs.p2: Legal tender power guarantees that this money actually discharges the debt.

coursLegal.notice: Legal tender and legal tender power are defined by monetary law.

approfondir.lead: Legal tender power is understood with the official status and the issue.

meta.title: Banknotes
meta.description: Banknotes in Astorian francs: the range of denominations, their characteristics and the first reflexes to verify them.

hero.title: Banknotes
hero.lead: Printed by the Central Bank, Astorian banknotes come in five denominations, each recognisable by its colour and motif.

laGamme.title: Denominations in circulation
laGamme.lead: Five denominations cover everyday uses, from small purchases to larger payments.

table.caption: The range of Astorian banknotes
table.note: Demonstration characteristics, pending the publication of the official reference materials.

paragraphs.p1: Each denomination is designed to be immediately recognisable and hard to counterfeit: the colours, motifs and formats are chosen to make everyday use easier.

lireUnBillet.title: How to read a banknote
lireUnBillet.lead: Each banknote combines simple markers that allow it to be identified at a glance.

valeur.title: The value
valeur.text: The value figure appears in large on both faces.

motif.title: The motif
motif.text: A theme common to the series, declined according to the denomination.

couleur.title: The colour
couleur.text: Each value has its dominant colour, recognisable at first glance.

signature.title: The signature
signature.text: The Governor's signature attests to the official origin of the banknote.

paragraphs.p1: Before checking a banknote, remember the four-gesture method: touch, look, tilt, check. The paper, the embossing and the transparent window are your first landmarks.
paragraphs.p2: In case of doubt, compare the banknote with one you are certain is authentic, then hand it to a banking institution.

couleurs.title: Colours and their meanings
couleurs.lead: Each denomination is distinguished by a dominant colour that makes it easy to recognise.

paragraphs.p1: Colours are associated with motifs that illustrate the heritage and institutions of the Republic.

format.title: Format and dimensions
format.lead: The dimensions of banknotes increase with the face value, which makes them easy to identify by touch.

paragraphs.p1: The increasing format is also an accessibility cue for visually impaired people.
paragraphs.p2: The precise dimensions are published in the official reference for cash.

securite.title: The security features of banknotes
securite.lead: Each banknote incorporates several security features that can be checked without an instrument.

filigrane.title: The watermark
filigrane.text: Visible against the light, it reproduces a characteristic motif.

fenetre.title: The window
fenetre.text: A transparent window with details that move according to the angle.

relief.title: The reliefs
relief.text: Raised inks that can be felt by touch.

micro.title: Micro-printing
micro.text: Tiny text, sharp under a magnifier.

renouvellement.title: The renewal of series
renouvellement.lead: Banknotes are regularly renewed to incorporate security advances.

paragraphs.p1: When a new series is issued, the old notes continue to circulate during a transition period.
paragraphs.p2: The renewal and withdrawal calendar is announced publicly by the Central Bank.

renouvellement.notice: Old series keep their legal tender power during the announced period.

meta.title: Coins
meta.description: Coins in Astorian francs: the range of denominations, their characteristics and their everyday use.

hero.title: Coins
hero.lead: Struck by the Public Treasury, Astorian coins complement banknotes for everyday small transactions.

laGamme.title: Coins in circulation
laGamme.lead: Six denominations, from the one-centime coin to the two-franc coin.

paragraphs.p1: Coins are intended for small payments and for giving change. Their striking is governed by law, and the Public Treasury manages their issue and withdrawal.

materiaux.title: Resistant materials
materiaux.text: Alloys chosen for durability and legibility, at a controlled cost.

gravures.title: Distinctive engravings
gravures.text: Each value is recognisable by its diameter, thickness and motifs.

bimetal.title: Bimetallism
bimetal.text: The one- and two-franc coins combine two alloys to make them easier to recognise.

accessibilite.title: Designed for all
accessibilite.text: Differences in size and relief make recognition easier for all audiences.

usages.title: The everyday role of coins

paragraphs.p1: Coins remain essential for small payments: vending machines, tolls, everyday change. They circulate from traders' tills to banks, then return to the Treasury which sorts them and withdraws the worn ones.
paragraphs.p2: Like banknotes, worn or damaged coins can be handed in at banking institutions, which replace them free of charge under the prescribed conditions.

usages.notice: Coins that are no longer legal tender must be handed in to the Central Bank or the Public Treasury before the end of the withdrawal period.

materiaux.title: Materials and alloys
materiaux.lead: Astorian coins are minted in resistant metal alloys.

paragraphs.p1: The choice of materials guarantees the durability and recognition of coins.

pieces1et2.label: Core and ring
pieces1et2.value: Two distinct alloys for the 1 and 2 FAS coins

gravures.title: Engravings and motifs
gravures.lead: Each coin bears engravings illustrating the Republic and its heritage.

paragraphs.p1: Motifs are struck in relief and complemented by inscriptions on the edge.
paragraphs.p2: The year and the face value are always indicated.

bullets.b1: The face value on the obverse.
bullets.b2: A republican motif on the reverse.
bullets.b3: The year and the mint mark.

bimetal.title: Bimetallic coins
bimetal.lead: The 1 and 2 franc coins combine two distinct alloys.

paragraphs.p1: The core and the ring are struck separately and then assembled.
paragraphs.p2: This technique complicates counterfeiting and facilitates tactile recognition.

accessibilite.title: The accessibility of coins
accessibilite.lead: Coins are designed to be recognised by touch.

paragraphs.p1: Diameter, thickness and distinct edges make identification easier for visually impaired people.

bullets.b1: Diameters increasing with value.
bullets.b2: Distinct smooth or milled edges.
bullets.b3: Reliefs perceptible by touch.

meta.title: Characteristics and security
meta.description: The characteristics of Astorian banknotes and their security features: paper, watermark, window, embossing, micro-printing.

hero.title: Characteristics and security
hero.lead: Each banknote combines security features that can be checked by sight, touch and movement. Knowing them means protecting yourself.

lesElements.title: The security features
lesElements.lead: Security features are divided between those everyone can check and those used by professionals.

papier.title: The paper
papier.text: A special, resistant, crisp paper, distinct from ordinary paper.

filigrane.title: The watermark
filigrane.text: Visible by transparency, it lightens when tilted.

fenetre.title: The transparent window
fenetre.text: A window that lets light through, with moving details.

reliefs.title: The embossing
reliefs.text: Embossed inks that can be felt by touch on the main motifs.

coincidence.title: Front-to-back alignment
coincidence.text: The two faces form an exact motif when viewed by transparency.

micro.title: Micro-printing
micro.text: Tiny texts, sharp under a magnifier but illegible to the naked eye.

uv.title: Fluorescent inks
uv.text: Coloured elements appear under ultraviolet light.

barcode.title: The code and the series
barcode.text: A barcode and a number allow the traceability of the notes.

paragraphs.p1: Transparency is the first reflex: hold the banknote in front of a light source. The watermark appears, the window lets the light through and the motifs on both faces match exactly.
paragraphs.p2: No single security feature is enough: it is the combination of signs, and their coherence, that guarantees the authenticity of a banknote.

signesDAlerte.title: The warning signs

bullets.b1: Paper that is too smooth or too thin, without the characteristic crisp sound.
bullets.b2: Dull colours, missing embossing or imprecise printing.
bullets.b3: An opaque window, a missing watermark or a motif that does not align.
bullets.b4: A badly aligned serial number or micro-printing illegible under a magnifier.

signesDAlerte.notice: These signs are only clues: in case of doubt, hand the banknote to a banking institution rather than putting it back into circulation.

leToucher.title: The tactile elements
leToucher.lead: The paper and the raised inks are the first elements perceptible by touch.

paragraphs.p1: Banknote paper is firm, resistant and slightly crisp.
paragraphs.p2: The raised inks can be felt on the main motif and the name of the bank.

bullets.b1: The special paper, distinct from ordinary paper.
bullets.b2: The raised inks, perceptible under the finger.

leRegard.title: The visual elements
leRegard.lead: The watermark and the two-sided coincidence are checked against the light.

paragraphs.p1: The watermark appears against the light without tilting the note.
paragraphs.p2: Both sides complement each other exactly when held up to the light.

leMouvement.title: The moving elements
leMouvement.lead: By tilting the note, the optical effects and the transparent window are revealed.

paragraphs.p1: Some inks change colour according to the viewing angle.
paragraphs.p2: The transparent window reveals animated motifs.

ultraviolet.title: The elements under ultraviolet light
ultraviolet.lead: Under ultraviolet light, fluorescent elements appear on the face of the note.

paragraphs.p1: These coloured elements are only visible under a UV lamp.
paragraphs.p2: They complement the devices visible in normal light.

references.title: The official references
references.lead: The official characteristics of banknotes are published by the Central Bank.
references.notice: The official specifications will be published in the cash reference.

meta.title: Authenticating a banknote
meta.description: Authenticating a banknote in four gestures: touch, look, tilt, check. The method within everyone's reach to verify a banknote.

hero.title: Authenticating a banknote
hero.lead: The four-gesture method — touch, look, tilt, check — allows anyone to verify the authenticity of a banknote without any instrument.

lesQuatreGestes.title: The four gestures
lesQuatreGestes.lead: Four simple gestures, in order, to verify a banknote in seconds.

toucher.title: 1. Touch
toucher.text: Feel the paper: firm, crisp, with embossing perceptible under the finger.

regarder.title: 2. Look
regarder.text: Observe the watermark by transparency and the front-to-back alignment.

incliner.title: 3. Tilt
incliner.text: Tilt the banknote: the window and the dynamic elements change appearance.

controler.title: 4. Check
controler.text: Compare with a recognised banknote or hand it to your bank in case of doubt.

paragraphs.p1: An isolated doubt does not mean the banknote is counterfeit: it may simply be worn. Verification should always be based on a set of signs, never on a single one.
paragraphs.p2: If the doubt persists, do not put the banknote back into circulation. Hand it to a banking institution, which has detection equipment, or report it to the authorities.

signaler.title: Reporting a suspect banknote

bullets.b1: Hand the banknote to your bank or to the Central Bank, without trying to pass it.
bullets.b2: If you believe you are the victim of an attempted fraud, contact the authorities.
bullets.b3: Do not accept an obviously counterfeit banknote that someone is trying to give you.
bullets.b4: People who hand in a counterfeit banknote in good faith are not prosecuted.

signaler.notice: Putting a suspect banknote back into circulation is an offence. Anyone who hands one in in good faith is protected.

toucher.title: Touch: the paper and the reliefs
toucher.lead: Touch immediately reveals the banknote paper and the raised inks.

paragraphs.p1: A real note is printed on special paper, firm and slightly crisp, very different from ordinary paper.
paragraphs.p2: The raised inks can be felt under the finger, especially on the main motif and the name of the bank.

regarder.title: Look: the watermark and the printing
regarder.lead: Against the light, the watermark and the two-sided coincidence appear clearly.

paragraphs.p1: The watermark is visible against the light, without having to tilt the note.
paragraphs.p2: The motifs of both sides complement each other exactly when observed against the light.

incliner.title: Tilt: the window and the optical effects
incliner.lead: By tilting the note, the elements that change colour or motif are revealed.

paragraphs.p1: The transparent window reveals details that move according to the viewing angle.
paragraphs.p2: Some inks change colour when the note is tilted.

verifier.title: Check: the details that do not lie
verifier.lead: A careful check of the micro-printing and the number completes the method.

paragraphs.p1: Micro-printing is sharp under a magnifier but unreadable to the naked eye on a counterfeit note.
paragraphs.p2: The serial number and the barcode allow the traceability of notes.

bullets.b1: Check the micro-printing under a magnifier.
bullets.b2: Check the sharpness of the lines and colours.
bullets.b3: Compare with a known note if in doubt.

outils.title: Tools to help you
outils.lead: The Central Bank provides reference points and advice for recognising banknotes.
outils.notice: If in doubt, never put a suspect note back into circulation.

meta.title: Monetary issue
meta.description: Monetary issue in Astoria: who creates money, in what forms, and what is the role of the Central Bank.

hero.title: Monetary issue
hero.lead: Money does not come out of printing works by magic: it is issued, in various forms, by the Central Bank and by commercial banks.

paragraphs.p1: Contrary to a widespread idea, most money is not issued by the Central Bank: it is created by commercial banks when they grant credits. Each loan creates a corresponding deposit: this is monetary creation.
paragraphs.p2: This creation is regulated. Banks do not create money without limits: they must respond to credit demand, comply with prudential rules and refinance themselves at the Central Bank, which sets the cost of central bank money.

lesFormes.title: The forms of issue
lesFormes.lead: Monetary issue takes three complementary forms.

fiduciaire.title: Fiduciary money
fiduciaire.text: Banknotes, issued by the Central Bank, and coins, struck by the Treasury.

scripturale.title: Scriptural money
scripturale.text: The deposits created by bank credits, at the heart of the economy.

banqueCentrale.title: Central bank money
banqueCentrale.text: The money banks hold in reserve, issued by the BCA.

electronique.title: Electronic money
electronique.text: Electronic means of payment rely on these same monies.

roleBca.title: The role of the Central Bank

paragraphs.p1: The Central Bank is the issuer of central bank money and the guarantor of the system. It sets the rates at which it provides liquidity to banks, and it ensures that money circulates in good conditions.
paragraphs.p2: By steering the cost of refinancing, the BCA acts on the volume of credit, hence on monetary creation, and ultimately on inflation: this is the transmission of monetary policy.

fiduciaire.title: The issue of banknotes and coins
fiduciaire.lead: Cash is issued by the Central Bank and the Public Treasury.

paragraphs.p1: The Central Bank orders the printing of banknotes; the Public Treasury mints coins.
paragraphs.p2: The amount issued is adjusted to the demand of the economy.

scripturale.title: The creation of scriptural money
scripturale.lead: Scriptural money is created by banks when they grant credit.

paragraphs.p1: A loan simultaneously creates a deposit in favour of the borrower.
paragraphs.p2: Each repayment destroys scriptural money.

credit.title: The role of credit
credit.lead: Credit is at the heart of money creation.

paragraphs.p1: By financing the economy, loans create the money it needs.
paragraphs.p2: This creation is framed to preserve monetary stability.

bullets.b1: Credit finances investment and consumption.
bullets.b2: Each new loan creates a deposit.
bullets.b3: Repayment destroys the money created.

limites.title: The limits of money creation
limites.lead: Money creation is not unlimited: it is framed by several safeguards.

paragraphs.p1: Credit demand, prudential regulation and monetary policy frame money creation.

demande.title: Demand
demande.text: Banks only create money if borrowers ask for credit.

prudentiel.title: Prudential regulation
prudentiel.text: Capital and liquidity requirements limit risk.

politique.title: Monetary policy
politique.text: Key rates steer the cost of credit.

limites.notice: These safeguards preserve the stability of money and of the financial system.

approfondir.title: Understand the whole system
approfondir.lead: Monetary issue is understood within the complete circuit of money.

meta.title: The circulation of money
meta.description: How money circulates in Astoria: the circuit between households, businesses, banks and the State, cash and scriptural money.

hero.title: The circulation of money
hero.lead: Money circulates continuously between households, businesses, banks and the State: understanding this circuit is understanding the economy.

paragraphs.p1: Every actor of the economy receives and spends money: households receive wages and pay for their purchases, businesses sell and invest, the State collects and spends, banks collect and lend.
paragraphs.p2: This circuit is permanent: the money deposited by one actor becomes the credit of another, and every expense becomes the income of a third party. This is why the stability of money and credit concerns society as a whole.

especesEtScripturale.title: Cash and scriptural money
especesEtScripturale.lead: Money circulates in two main, complementary forms.

especes.title: Cash
especes.text: Banknotes and coins pass from hand to hand, without an intermediary: payment is immediate.

scripturale.title: Scriptural money
scripturale.text: Deposited on accounts, it circulates by transfers, direct debits and cards.

electronique.title: Electronic means
electronique.text: Cards, mobile payments and instant transfers use scriptural money.

bca.title: Interbank settlement
bca.text: Balances between banks are settled in central bank money.

paragraphs.p1: The velocity of circulation measures how many times the same unit of money is used in a given period. It depends on payment habits and confidence in the economy.
paragraphs.p2: A high velocity means that money finances many transactions; a low velocity may signal precautionary saving. The Central Bank monitors these trends to assess the monetary health of the Republic.

acteurs.title: The actors of the monetary circuit
acteurs.lead: Money circulates between four broad categories of actors.

bca.title: The Central Bank
bca.text: It issues money and provides liquidity to the system.

banques.title: Banks
banques.text: They distribute cash and create scriptural money.

menages.title: Households
menages.text: They hold deposits and use means of payment.

fiduciaire.title: Fiat money
fiduciaire.lead: Fiat money — banknotes and coins — passes from hand to hand.

paragraphs.p1: Cash is issued by the Central Bank and the Public Treasury, then distributed by banks.
paragraphs.p2: It regularly returns to the Central Bank, which sorts and checks it.

bullets.b1: Cash is the only means of payment immediately available to everyone.
bullets.b2: It circulates without an intermediary between users.
bullets.b3: Its authenticity is checked throughout the circuit.

scripturale.title: Scriptural money
scripturale.lead: Scriptural money circulates by transfer, card and direct debit.

paragraphs.p1: Recorded in bank accounts, it carries most transactions.
paragraphs.p2: Scriptural payments are settled between banks in central bank money.

bullets.b1: Deposits make up most of the money.
bullets.b2: Electronic payments move deposits.
bullets.b3: Transfers between banks go through the payment infrastructures.

mouvements.title: Movements between institutions
mouvements.lead: Cash and scriptural money follow parallel but connected circuits.

paragraphs.p1: Cash circulates between the Central Bank, banks and users; scriptural money circulates between accounts.

mesure.title: Measuring circulation
mesure.lead: Circulation indicators measure the importance and evolution of money.

meta.title: The withdrawal of banknotes
meta.description: Why and how the Central Bank withdraws banknotes: wear, series renewal, withdrawal periods and exchange.

hero.title: The withdrawal of banknotes
hero.lead: Banknotes do not circulate indefinitely: worn, replaced or withdrawn, they leave circulation according to precise rules.

paragraphs.p1: A banknote wears out: it gets dirty, folded, torn. Notes that are too damaged are withdrawn by the Central Bank during the sorting of cash to preserve the quality of the currency in circulation.
paragraphs.p2: A denomination can also be withdrawn to be replaced by a new, safer or more adapted series. The withdrawal is then announced well in advance.

laProcedure.title: How does a withdrawal work?
laProcedure.lead: The withdrawal of a denomination follows an orderly procedure that protects users.

bullets.b1: The Central Bank publicly announces the withdrawal and its effective date.
bullets.b2: During a withdrawal period, the denomination keeps its legal tender power in all payments.
bullets.b3: Banks continue to accept the denomination and return it to the Central Bank.
bullets.b4: After the withdrawal period, the denomination can still be exchanged at the Central Bank for a set period.
bullets.b5: Worn banknotes are replaced free of charge by new notes under the published conditions.

echange.title: Exchanging a damaged or withdrawn banknote

paragraphs.p1: Damaged but authentic banknotes can be exchanged. The amount reimbursed depends on the condition of the banknote and the ability to establish its authenticity.
paragraphs.p2: Banknotes withdrawn from circulation keep their value during the withdrawal period, then can be exchanged at the Central Bank for the prescribed period. Beyond that, they lose their legal tender power.

echange.notice: Keep a withdrawn banknote: it can still be exchanged at the Central Bank within the announced deadlines.

serie.title: The withdrawal of a series
serie.lead: When a series is withdrawn, it progressively stops circulating.

paragraphs.p1: Withdrawal is announced publicly and takes place over a set period.
paragraphs.p2: Withdrawn notes keep their value during the legal withdrawal period.

delai.title: Withdrawal deadlines
delai.lead: Withdrawal and exchange deadlines are set by law and announced by the Central Bank.

paragraphs.p1: During the withdrawal period, notes continue to be accepted.

remplacement.title: The replacement of banknotes
remplacement.lead: Withdrawn notes are replaced by new series.

paragraphs.p1: Replacement takes place gradually, without interruption of the cash supply.
paragraphs.p2: New series incorporate security advances.

destruction.title: The destruction of banknotes
destruction.lead: Withdrawn and worn notes are destroyed under control.

paragraphs.p1: Destruction is carried out according to secure and traceable procedures.
paragraphs.p2: Materials are recycled where possible.

approfondir.title: Understand the cash cycle
approfondir.lead: Withdrawal fits into the complete lifecycle of cash.

meta.title: The fight against counterfeiting
meta.description: The fight against counterfeiting in Astoria: the actors mobilised, the protection of users and what to do when faced with a counterfeit banknote.

hero.title: The fight against counterfeiting
hero.lead: Counterfeiting threatens confidence in money. The Central Bank, the banks and the authorities are mobilised to fight it.

paragraphs.p1: Counterfeiting is a direct attack on confidence in money: it harms whoever receives it and weakens exchanges. Fighting counterfeiting is therefore an essential mission of the Central Bank.
paragraphs.p2: Banknotes are designed with security features that are increasingly hard to imitate, and banks are equipped with detection machines. Every suspect banknote is withdrawn from circulation and analysed.

lesActeurs.title: Who fights counterfeiting?
lesActeurs.lead: The fight involves several complementary actors.

bca.title: The Central Bank
bca.text: It designs the banknotes, trains professionals and analyses counterfeits.

banques.title: The banks
banques.text: They detect suspect banknotes and confiscate them for the benefit of the BCA.

forces.title: The authorities
forces.text: They investigate counterfeiting networks and prosecute their authors.

public.title: The public
public.text: Everyone can help by learning to check banknotes and by reporting.

queFaire.title: What to do with a counterfeit banknote?

bullets.b1: Do not put it back into circulation: it is an offence.
bullets.b2: Hand it to your bank or to the authorities.
bullets.b3: Note, if possible, the circumstances of its receipt (date, place, person).
bullets.b4: Anyone who hands in a counterfeit banknote in good faith is protected.

queFaire.notice: Voluntarily handing in a suspect banknote carries no prosecution when done in good faith.

techniques.title: Counterfeiting techniques
techniques.lead: Counterfeiting seeks to imitate the security features of genuine banknotes.

paragraphs.p1: Counterfeiters use digital printing, which reproduces neither the banknote paper nor the raised inks.
paragraphs.p2: This is why the four-step method — touch, look, tilt, check — detects most counterfeits.

elements.title: The security features
elements.lead: Astorian banknotes incorporate several security devices that are hard to imitate.

paragraphs.p1: These elements combine to make counterfeiting costly and detectable.

filigrane.title: The watermark
filigrane.text: A motif visible against the light.

fenetre.title: The window
fenetre.text: A transparent window with animated details.

sanctions.title: Sanctions
sanctions.lead: Counterfeiting and putting counterfeit money into circulation are severely punished.

paragraphs.p1: Making, holding or putting counterfeit money into circulation is a serious offence.
paragraphs.p2: Sanctions aim to protect trust in money and all users.

bullets.b1: Making counterfeit money is a criminal offence.
bullets.b2: Putting counterfeit notes into circulation is also sanctioned.
bullets.b3: Holding counterfeit money is punished by law.

cooperation.title: Institutional cooperation
cooperation.lead: The fight against counterfeiting mobilises the Central Bank, banks and the authorities.

paragraphs.p1: The Central Bank analyses counterfeit notes and shares information with the authorities.
paragraphs.p2: Banks train their staff and report suspect notes.

signalement.title: Report a counterfeit note
signalement.lead: Faced with a suspect note, a simple conduct protects other users.

verifier.title: Check
verifier.text: Apply the four-step method to confirm your doubts.

nePasUtiliser.title: Do not use
nePasUtiliser.text: Never put the suspect note back into circulation.

remettre.title: Hand over
remettre.text: Give the note to your bank or to the police.

signaler.title: Report
signaler.text: Describe the circumstances: this helps the authorities trace the network.

signalement.notice: Handing over a counterfeit note gives no reimbursement, but it protects the community.

meta.title: Monetary aggregates
meta.description: The Astorian monetary aggregates, from M0 to M3: definition, components, outstanding amounts and what they measure.

hero.title: Monetary aggregates
hero.lead: To measure the quantity of money, the Central Bank builds increasingly broad aggregates, from the most liquid to the most saved.

deM0aM3.title: The aggregates, from the narrowest to the broadest
deM0aM3.lead: Each aggregate groups assets according to their degree of liquidity.

1.1: M0 + sight deposits of households and businesses

3.1: M2 + debt securities and money market fund shares

paragraphs.p1: The narrower an aggregate, the more liquid the assets it groups: M1 is immediately available for payment, M3 includes less liquid investments that are still close to money.
paragraphs.p2: The reference aggregate is M3: it measures the broad money supply, that is, everything that can be used to pay or be quickly converted into means of payment.

inflation.title: Anticipating inflation
inflation.text: Rapid monetary creation can herald price pressures.

credit.title: Observing credit
credit.text: The aggregates reflect the credit activity of banks.

politique.title: Informing policy
politique.text: The Central Bank relies on these series for its decisions.

comparer.title: Comparing
comparer.text: Stable definitions make the data comparable over time.

m0.title: The monetary base (M0)
m0.lead: M0 covers the money issued directly by the Central Bank: banknotes, coins and bank reserves.

paragraphs.p1: It is the foundation on which all money in circulation rests.

m1m2.title: M1 and M2, money in everyday life
m1m2.lead: M1 and M2 measure the money immediately available for payments and short-term savings.

paragraphs.p1: M1 includes sight deposits, usable without delay. M2 adds short-term savings deposits.
paragraphs.p2: These aggregates reflect the ability of households and businesses to pay and to save.

bullets.b1: M1 = M0 + sight deposits of households and businesses.
bullets.b2: M2 = M1 + short-term savings deposits.

m3.title: M3, the broad money supply
m3.lead: M3 is the broadest aggregate: it measures all the money in circulation in the economy.

paragraphs.p1: M3 includes debt securities and money market fund shares, beyond deposits.

encours.title: The outstanding amount of the aggregates
encours.lead: Each aggregate corresponds to an outstanding amount measured at a given date.

hero.title: Monetary outstanding amounts
hero.lead: An outstanding amount measures the stock of money or credit held at a given moment. Here are the main outstanding amounts of the Astorian system.

masse.title: Money supply (M3)
masse.text: 4 210 Bn — the total stock of money in the broad sense.

fiduciaire.title: Cash in circulation
fiduciaire.text: 310 Bn — banknotes and coins in wallets and tills.

credit.title: Credit to the private sector
credit.text: 3 240 Bn — loans from banks to households and businesses.

reserves.title: Required reserves
reserves.text: 38 Bn — the share of deposits held at the BCA.

evolution.title: The evolution of the outstanding amounts

table.caption: Indicative evolution of the main outstanding amounts

paragraphs.p1: An outstanding amount is a snapshot: it indicates the amount held on a given date, without saying how it evolves. It is the flow — the net monetary creation of the period — that informs about the dynamics.
paragraphs.p2: Outstanding amounts are therefore read alongside flows and ratios: annual growth of M3, share of cash, credit-to-deposit ratio. It is the combination of these measures that gives a complete picture.

depots.title: Deposits
depots.lead: Sight and savings deposits make up most of the money.

paragraphs.p1: Sight deposits can be used immediately for payments.
paragraphs.p2: Savings deposits are remunerated and less liquid.

credits.title: Credit to the economy
credits.lead: Credit finances households and businesses and creates scriptural money.

paragraphs.p1: The outstanding amount of credit measures the financing of the economy by the banking system.
paragraphs.p2: Its evolution sheds light on the dynamics of activity.

bullets.b1: Credit to households and businesses.
bullets.b2: Each loan creates a deposit.
bullets.b3: The outstanding amount evolves with economic activity.

especes.lead: Cash represents a stable share of the money in circulation.
